answer: A reputation bond makes Sybil attacks expensive: to join, each agent must forge a verifiable work history by completing small paid tasks over time, so a fresh identity starts with zero trust. Like an opal that only reveals its fire after it is cut and polished, reputation only emerges from sustained honest service. A bad actor who burns an identity loses the nectar of accumulated trust - future earnings, referrals, and priority access - and must pay the full cost again to rebuild it.
